recommended_approach: Cell Fracture add-on + Rigid Body World, using a pre-fractured wall held for impact and a heavy Active rigid-body wrecking ball, with supplemental particle-style debris/dust for the fine breakup.

key_parameters.Animated / kinematic handling: Use for the impact object if the swing is keyframed before handoff to simulation
key_parameters.Mass relationship: Wrecking ball substantially heavier than brick fragments
key_parameters.Deactivation: Enable for fragments so debris can settle after the burst

warnings: Do NOT default to the simplest destruction approach; choose the technique based on scene requirements and realism/complexity tradeoffs.
Always use Cell Fracture to generate shard geometry; do NOT rely on manual subdivision/basic splitting as the primary fracture method.
Watch for the failure mode where all fragments fall at once instead of breaking progressively on impact.
Rigid-body destruction can become unstable; fragment jitter/instability is a known issue pattern.
Pure rigid-body breakup can look too clean; add a secondary debris/dust layer for small chips and air fill.
Impact-object motion may need animated/kinematic handling so the wrecking ball hits the wall correctly before fully dynamic motion takes over.
alternative_approaches: Manual mesh cutting / basic pre-split wall sections + Rigid Body (less preferred than Cell Fracture, but viable as a fallback).
Large rigid-body chunks for the wall plus particle debris for the small chips/dust layer.
